# Answer

**They came in from the left-hand side of the frame — the near, lower-left end of the path.**

## What the path actually does

The single track that carries all the foreground traffic is one continuous
diagonal. Traced from the top of the picture downwards it:

1. enters at the **right edge** of the canvas as a pale roadway (at roughly
   two-thirds height, just under the ruined arched masonry on the right cliff);
2. crosses the **stone arch bridge** on the right, cresting where the horseman is;
3. drops left and forward onto the **wooden plank footbridge** with the rustic
   pole railing along its left (ravine) side;
4. continues as a bare earth ramp down toward the **lower left**, skirting the
   dark ravine with the stream, and runs off the bottom-left of the canvas.

So the path has two ends inside the frame: a far end at the right edge, and a
near end down in the lower left, in the immediate foreground.

Perspective confirms which end is near. The plank deck narrows as it goes up to
the right; the trestle supports and broken plank ends are at the lower-left end;
and the figures shrink with distance — the two foreground hounds are drawn at
roughly twice the scale of the traveler, and the traveler (about 54 px tall) is
noticeably larger in scale than the mounted figure beyond him. Depth increases
towards the upper right. The lower left is the near end.

## Which way the traveler is going

The traveler — the man in the broad-brimmed hat with the pale doublet, standing
where the planking meets the earth bank — is moving **away from us, up the bridge
to the right**. Every motion cue in the foreground agrees:

- **The two hounds on the footbridge are unmistakably galloping to the right.**
  In both animals the head is at the right-hand end: pointed muzzle, visible ear
  and raised neck, with the body strung out behind to the left, the tail curving
  up at the left end, the forelegs reaching forward-right and the hind legs
  thrown back to the left. They are in full extended gait toward the right, not
  merely looking that way.
- **The dog right at the traveler's feet reads the same way**, trotting alongside
  him with the body aligned along the path and the near end of the group
  trailing back down the slope.
- **The horseman ahead of him is riding right as well.** The pale rounded mass of
  the horse with its hind legs sits at the lower left of the animal, while a
  bright, tapering form — the horse's head and neck, at about the right height
  above the roadway — projects forward to the right; the rider's hat and head sit
  above and slightly behind (left of) that head, and his pale cloak falls away
  behind him to the left. That is a rider seen from behind, climbing away over
  the bridge.
- The traveler's own figure leans very slightly forward-right, as a walker does
  going up a grade, and the lit patch of his face/collar shows on the right-hand
  side, below the brim — he is looking up the path toward the horseman.

The whole group therefore reads as one party — a traveler or huntsman with four
hounds strung out behind him, following a horseman — all moving inward and
upward, out of the foreground and toward the right-hand edge.

## Therefore

Running that trajectory backwards, the traveler and the two dogs came up from the
**near, lower-left end of the path**: out of the bottom-left of the picture, along
the earth track beside the ravine and the wooden guard rail, onto the plank
footbridge where we now see them. They entered the scene from the **left side of
the frame**, and they are heading for the right — across the stone arch and out at
the right edge.

The right-hand edge, where the road plainly crosses the frame boundary above the
arch, is where they are *going*, not where they came from.

# Answer

The traveler walking next to the two dogs on the wooden footbridge in the lower foreground entered the scene from the **bottom** side of the frame (specifically near the **bottom-left** corner), traveling from **left to right**.

Depending on how "side of the frame" is defined, the answer can be specified as follows:

1. **Bottom Side of the Frame (Precise Path Intersection):** 
   If "side of the frame" refers to the literal border edge of the image where the path enters/terminates, they came from the **bottom side** (or **bottom edge**) of the frame. Tracing the path backwards from the footbridge, it descends diagonally to the lower left, ending directly at the bottom margin of the canvas where the rocky ledge is signed by the artist (*R. SAVERY*).

2. **Left / Bottom-Left Side of the Frame (Direction of Travel):**
   If "side of the frame" refers to the general direction of the scene from which their trajectory originates (since they are moving from left to right, uphill), they came from the **left** (or **bottom-left**) side of the frame. 

---

### Comprehensive Analysis & Justification

1. **Locating the Traveler and Dogs:**
   - In the lower foreground, there is a wooden footbridge composed of horizontal logs or wooden planks, with a wooden railing along its left-hand side.
   - On this wooden footbridge, a traveler wearing a light-colored (beige/white) coat and a dark wide-brimmed hat is walking uphill (from bottom-left toward top-right).
   - This traveler is walking with a walking stick and is accompanied by **two small dogs** (one white/spotted and one dark) walking right beside them.
   - Slightly ahead of them on the bridge, two brown dogs are running up the path toward the right.

2. **Tracing the Path and Trajectory Backwards:**
   - The traveler is moving from the lower-left towards the upper-right (heading towards the arched stone bridge on the right).
   - Reversing this trajectory to find where they entered the scene, we follow the path backwards (downwards and to the left).
   - The wooden steps of the footbridge lead down onto a natural rocky/sandy path in the lower foreground of the image.
   - This sandy/rocky path continues diagonally downward and to the left, running along the bottom edge of the frame.
   - At the bottom-center/bottom-left, the path terminates directly at the **bottom edge of the image frame** (on the rocky outcrop where Roelandt Savery's signature is located).

3. **Excluding Other Sides:**
   - **Left Edge:** Directly to the left of the sandy path is a deep, dark ravine/waterfall gorge. There is no path crossing the river or connecting to the left edge of the frame at this level. The left side of the frame consists of steep, impassable dark rocky cliffs and dense foliage.
   - **Right Edge:** The traveler is moving *towards* the right side of the frame, so they could not have entered from there.
   - **Top Edge:** The traveler is in the lower foreground, moving upwards, but their path originates from the bottom.

Thus, the traveler entered the scene from the **bottom** edge (near the **bottom-left** corner) of the frame.
